questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose University of Edinburgh because it is a well-respected university in a vibrant city with lots of opportunities to grow both personally and professionally, and I also liked that Edinburgh is well connected, making it easy to travel and explore other parts of the UK.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy to get the information I needed before arriving, as the university provided clear step-by-step guidance and it was always easy to contact staff (the visiting student office) with any questions I had before orientation.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Most of the information was explained clearly online, and any questions I had were answered quickly by the staff whenever I emailed them.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: After confirming my place at the university, I was able to apply for housing through the application website. I had to choose five accommodation options, and I was offered a place at one of them shortly after. Overall, the whole process was very straightforward and easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There are not really any "on campus" housing opportunities, as the university accommodations are spread throughout the city. It depends on where you are placed, but I only had around a 15–20 minute walk to class, and the public transportation in Edinburgh is also very easy to use.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Housing was perfectly fine. Some accommodations are of course nicer than others, but I lived in a flat with three other girls and we had our own shower, toilet, and kitchen. My room was also quite spacious, and I lived in an area with lots of other students, which made it easy to visit friends and socialize.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Quite straightforward. Most of the steps and deadlines were explained clearly online, and I received emails with instructions about what I needed to complete before and after arriving.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The university staff were easy to contact by email and answered questions quickly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to register for some of the classes I wanted, but many of the more interesting courses were unfortunately not available to visiting students, which was a bit disappointing.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My advice would be to register for classes as early as possible, since many courses fill up very quickly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The teachers were great, but I felt that the academic level at University of Copenhagen was higher than at University of Edinburgh, especially in the first-year courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: As a film student, I liked that many of the classes were more hands-on compared to the ones at my home university.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Undergraduate Course: Music 1A: Psychology of Music (MUSI08069)
- Undergraduate Course: Medieval Afterlives: Music and Cultural Imagination (MUSI10101)
- Undergraduate Course: Soundtracks for Screen (UG) (MUSI10112)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Music 1A: Psychology of Music (MUSI08069) was very interesting, and the teacher was super engaging and fun to listen to. However, the academic level felt quite low compared to what I was used to at University of Copenhagen.

Soundtracks for Screen (UG) (MUSI10112) was a course for both third-year BA and MA students. I really enjoyed the course overall, but I sometimes felt that the teacher expected too much from visiting students, since many of the other students had already taken his class the previous semester and were familiar with material I had not previously studied.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Apart from my personal spending on things like going out, clothes, and toiletries, I also spent quite a bit of money on travelling. I made many international friends during my exchange, and we often travelled together to different places, so a good amount of my budget went toward plane tickets and trips.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In general, the city is much cheaper than Copenhagen, and it is definitely possible to budget well when it comes to food while still eating well. There are also many places around the city that offer student discounts and deals.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were lots and lots of clubs and societies for all kinds of interests, so it was very easy to find activities and meet people with similar hobbies.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely take the opportunity to explore Scotland, especially the Scottish Highlands, they are absolutely gorgeous! I would also recommend visiting Glasgow, or renting a car with friends and travelling down to England or Wales. There is so much to see and do, and travelling around the UK during exchange was one of the most fun parts of the experience.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There were lots of opportunities for day trips and weekend travel. I went to Glasgow a couple of times, and once I travelled to Cardiff to watch a rugby match. Some of my friends also took the bus to London for weekend trips, so it was very easy to explore different parts of the UK.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I am from Irish heritage and have grown up around the culture, so I can’t fully speak for others, but from what I saw my international friends adjusted very quickly. The people here are very friendly and always willing to help, which makes settling in much easier.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn’t find any major cultural differences particularly challenging, and overall it was quite easy to adjust. If anything, there were only small differences in academic expectations and teaching style compared to what I was used to, but nothing that caused real difficulties in settling in or adapting.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated how friendly and welcoming people were, as well as the strong student culture in the city. There were always lots of events, societies and social opportunities.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: First, make sure to apply for classes early, as many fill up quickly and options for exchange students can be limited. Second, take advantage of student life and societies, as there are lots of opportunities to meet people and get involved. Third, make sure to dress appropriately for the weather, as it can get quite cold and wet!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: One extra thing that might be useful is to be open-minded and proactive in the beginning, since it can take a little time to figure out course options, housing, and how everything works. Once you do, though, everything is well organised and support is easy to access. Also, getting involved in student societies early really helps you settle in and meet people quickly. I used the student website "learn" to write to other exchange students to meet up.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was making so many lifelong friendships!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was feeling homesick at the beginning, which is quite normal when you first move abroad. However, once I settled in and got involved in student life, it quickly became much easier. You end up enjoying it so much that you won’t want to leave!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
